title: Refuse a bad shipment where the feed hands it over

blocks.text: The warehouse takes shipments from a carrier's feed in the afternoon, and the dispatch run prints the pallet sheets at night. Last week the dispatch run stopped on a shipment with no destination, and nobody could tell which feed message it came from. The week before, a shipment of zero parcels printed a sheet with nothing on it, and a pallet left unlabelled.
`Shipment` already stores what the feed sends and prints its routing code. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Shipment.java`:

items: `requireFields(...)`: a shipment needs a tracking id that isn't blank, a destination, and between 1 and 20 parcels;

blocks.text: When you're done, a shipment the dispatch run couldn't handle is refused when the feed creates it: a missing value with a `NullPointerException`, a present but unusable one with an `IllegalArgumentException`. Every label is present, and the feed can't change an accepted shipment's labels afterwards. About six lines in total.

cases.says: a complete shipment is accepted with its values, labels and routing code as sent
shipments of 1 and of 20 parcels are accepted
a missing destination is refused by the constructor, not later when the routing code is printed
an empty or blank tracking id is refused, not only a null one
a parcel count of 0, 21 or a negative number is refused
the shipment keeps its own copy of the labels, so the feed changing its list later changes nothing
a null label, or no label list at all, is refused by the constructor

origin.section: A Check in the Constructor Puts the Caller in the Trace

concepts: Checking arguments in the constructor (null, blank, range) throws while the code that holds the bad value is on the stack, so the trace names the caller.
A constructor check on a list holds only if the object keeps its own copy: an unmodifiable view shows the caller's later changes, and List.copyOf copies and rejects null elements.
A value that is present but out of range fails nowhere: the code that uses it computes a wrong result.
